sectors.name: Pit straight and T1–3
sectors.observed: Long white pit buildings face a covered red crowd stand, with bright paired floodlights and yellow pit-edge paint. The first complex has close mesh fences, individual red-white kerbs and paved escape lanes. The actual driver-LEFT pit footprint crosses native zero, approximately4769→163m in the corrected frame. The old4896m center label is historical and superseded.

sectors.name: Republic Boulevard T4–5
sectors.observed: The Republic Boulevard walls and mesh sit close to the asphalt. Palms, broadleaf crowns and pale modern facades appear behind them. Long rows of floodlights continue overhead. Urban road markings and paved verges should remain visible.
sectors.registration: Approximate sector association from road shape, map and landmarks, not linear playback time. Bounds are authoring intervals, not surveyed corner boundaries.

sectors.name: Raffles Boulevard T6–7
sectors.observed: Glass office and hotel facades have repeated window mullions. Large yellow hatched junctions, city lamps and close barriers define Raffles Boulevard. Millenia, Suntec and Marina Square use their mapped positions, with trees breaking up the building walls. Direct 632/634/636 s continues through T7 and the T7–T8 straight, with the temporary Stamford spectators close on driver RIGHT.
sectors.registration: Approximate sector association from road shape, map and landmarks, not linear playback time. Bounds are authoring intervals, not surveyed corner boundaries.

sectors.name: Stamford, Padang and T8–T10
sectors.observed: The Old City Hall colonnade and former Supreme Court give the Padang section its pale civic architecture. A broad lawn and mature tree canopy sit behind close fencing. Low cricket and recreation clubs face them. Kerbs and yellow junction marks remain distinct. Direct 638 s is RIGHT T8; 640–641 s faces toward T9 with the rounded Swissôtel tower ahead/right above the 30 m Raffles City podium.
sectors.registration: Approximate sector association from road shape, map and landmarks, not linear playback time. Bounds are authoring intervals, not surveyed corner boundaries.

sectors.name: Anderson Bridge and Fullerton hairpin
sectors.observed: Anderson Bridge has narrow masonry edges and balustrades. Fullerton and the Waterboat House frame the riverfront turns, with heavy cornices, tall bays and trees. Escape areas remain paved beside these river walls.
sectors.registration: Approximate sector association from road shape, map and landmarks, not linear playback time. Bounds are authoring intervals, not surveyed corner boundaries.

sectors.name: Esplanade Drive and Connaught
sectors.observed: Esplanade Drive and Connaught are broad paved streets beside grandstands and dense trees. The two spiked Esplanade shells sit beyond the route, with tall office towers and distant marina buildings above the floodlights. Asphalt and wall bases must stay readable at night.
sectors.registration: Approximate sector association from road shape, map and landmarks, not linear playback time. Bounds are authoring intervals, not surveyed corner boundaries.
sectors.coverage_note: Direct EsplanadeDrive views afterT13. ActualT14/T15 corner poses remain unmatched; do not use646s asT14.

sectors.observed: Modern NS Square bypass/waterfront straight, continuous urban fencing and overhead race-light strings.1250.81s directly shows the Singapore Flyer rim/capsule ring ahead above the road; its white capsule points contrast with a dark rim/sky. Preserve the current19-turn layout without the removed old grandstand tunnel sequence.

sectors.name: Final corners and pit complex
sectors.observed: The Flyer wheel, low retail base, pit entry and terraces frame the final corners. Bright lights, compact red-white kerbs and yellow paved edges lead back to the white pit roof and main stand. Protection should follow the final curves continuously. Continuous 1254/1255/1255.8 s directly shows the ECP viaduct deck, underside beams and forked piers through the Flyer right/left sequence. The1257 s trackside cut is excluded as a matching cockpit pose.
